findings: All seven relaxed-budget proposals are supported; all eighteen distinct local roots are already retained after ordinary search.
Across eighteen local cases, selected-support compilation reduces compile time 75.30% and record bytes 86.16% versus full-context covers, with 5.45% more records.
Adding measured per-case preparation reverses the saving versus ordinary search on the original eleven-case subgroup. Controlled supplied-core cases also remain slower than ordinary solving.
Six changed-context expansions after cold reopen each reuse the core and add exactly one wrapper. Prior rows remain byte-identical.
limits: No minimum support, universal semantic canonical form, automatic-origin guarantee, whole-query gain, new Lean refinement or arbitrary-SAT polynomial bound.
Wrapper content grows with enclosing source size; cumulative history is preserved and supplemental banks are not automatically used as causal input.
next: Discover exact partial clause shortening by checked forced literals on unresolved contexts and fresh mixtures; retain proof support when adding derived binary consequences.
Use the selected-support compiler and persisted core reuse when composing those interactions; measure iterative discovery and live total costs before adoption.
policy: Keep optional; support-only compiler is validated offline, not a new live search default
